newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JONES CONFIRMS STATUS AS WORLD TITLE FAVOURITE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES CONFIRMS STATUS AS WORLD TITLE FAVOURITE.

text.p: American champion Marion Jones confirmed her status as world title favourite on Saturday by making a second round 100 metres victory look as easy as an evening stroll.
But the 21-year-old's relaxed appearance was deceptive.
The former basketball player looked to be cruising on a warm Athens evening as she won her heat in 10.96 seconds to reach Sunday's semifinals on the opening day of the world championships.
She confessed afterwards that she was tense inside as she prepared to bid for her first major title on Sunday evening.
"I have been waiting for ever for Sunday to come around," Jones said. "I probably won't get any sleep tonight. It will be the greatest moment of my career if I come away with a world title."
Jones was given a clear warning by the Ukraine's Zhanna Pintussevich that she has a tough task on her hands in the final.

Pintussevich, who clocked the fastest time in Saturday morning's first-round of 11.01, stepped up another gear in the evening to produce a national record 10.90 although she appeared to be working harder than the American.

The time was the fastest of the day and the second fastest performance in the world this year. Only Olympic champion Gail Devers, who is not running in the individual 100 here, has run faster this season although Jones has also clocked the same time.

Jamaican veteran Merlene Ottey, who has won more world championship medals than any other athlete but who is still seeking her first 100 gold, also looked in formidable form, winning her second-round heat easily in 11.00.
"It is not just going to be Ottey in the final. There are several other athletes who are ready to run fast," Jones said. "But I am ready to run sub-10.90."

Jones's time was the second fastest of the second round ahead of Ottey. The experienced Jamaican played down the significance of the first day's racing where both the men and women's 100 metres heats have shown that the Athens track is hard and fast.
"The track is very fast. But it doesn't matter what you do today. It is tomorrow that counts," the 37-year-old said.
